s1.syndrome_frame: A toddler with a chronic skin eruption characterized by multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale, accompanied by fever and otitis media
salient_findings: Multiple annular, indurated, dusky red plaques with central clearing and trailing scale
Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm on histopathology
Positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
key_facts: The patient is a toddler with a 2-month history of skin eruption
The eruption began with multiple round red patches that slowly increased in size
The patient has a medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and juvenile xanthogranulomas
The patient was treated with griseofulvin and clotrimazole without improvement
The patient developed fever and was diagnosed with otitis media one day prior to presentation
The patient is currently taking acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and amoxicillin
Scattered café au lait macules are present on the back
Histopathology showed a perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163
The white blood cell count is 76,400/µL

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate with positive CD33, CD123, and CD4 immunohistochemical staining

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's medical history and presence of café au lait macules

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multicentric disease with skin and possible systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Positive CD4 and CD163 immunohistochemical staining, consistent with histiocytic disease

shortlist.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, consistent with indeterminate cell morphology

raw.rationale: The patient's histopathology results showing a perivascular and periadnexal infiltrate of cells with homogeneous chromatin and abundant cytoplasm, along with positive immunohistochemical staining for CD33, CD123, CD4, and CD163, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Additionally, the patient's medical history of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and the presence of café au lait macules are also associated with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

rejected.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient's histopathology results do not match the typical findings of juvenile xanthogranuloma, which is a condition the patient already has in their medical history.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and clinical presentation are not typical for Erdheim-Chester disease, which usually affects adults and has a distinct set of systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: The patient's immunohistochemical staining results do not match the typical profile of Rosai-Dorfman disease, which is usually positive for S100 and CD1a.

rejected.label: Indeterminate cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: The patient's histopathology and immunohistochemical staining results are more consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis than indeterminate cell histiocytosis, which has a more variable and nonspecific immunophenotype.

gold: Leukemia cutis secondary to juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML)
